headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: OpenHands can write/browse/egress while mem0 lacks documented isolation, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP, so if mem0 content is surfaced into that workspace or via a shared channel, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so the interaction path exists, though not proven by default.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are copied into OpenHands files or MCP messages
IF OpenHands parses mem0-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep mem0 outputs in a separate workspace
Disable MCP channels between the agents
Add a manual review step before OpenHands acts on mem0 text
Prefix mem0 outputs as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands reads files in its runtime and can egress broadly, while mem0 is a memory system that may hold user content. If mem0 data is mounted into OpenHands or copied into its runtime, sensitive material can flow into a tool that can transmit context externally. mem0 has no documented data-class restrictions here, so the shared-workspace path is plausible.
conditions: IF mem0 stores sensitive notes that are mounted into OpenHands
IF OpenHands sends file contents or context to its configured model provider
mitigations: Do not mount mem0 storage into OpenHands
Use separate credentials and workspaces
Redact secrets before copying data across
Turn off network egress for the OpenHands runtime
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has unrestricted write access inside its runtime, can modify git state, and supports multiple instances via mounted volume only. mem0 is a knowledge-management system that may also persist state, so if both touch the same mounted files or repo, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite changes. The shared mutable-resource path is credible and defaults are not isolated enough.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted directory or git repository
IF OpenHands runs multiple instances against the same volume
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Snapshot the workspace before edits
requires-engineering: add runtime-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files, browser output, and MCP results, so if it consumes mem0-generated summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or external actions. mem0 is a memory layer rather than a verifier, and no verification boundary is documented between the pair. The pathway exists in default-style agent workflows, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses mem0 output as ground truth
IF OpenHands performs edits, browser actions, or subprocess actions based on that output
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Cross-check mem0 claims against source files
Mark mem0 output as advisory only
Log provenance for every acted-on claim
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands handles files in its runtime and can egress broadly, while mem0 is a memory store that may retain user data. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets are stored in mem0 and then mounted into OpenHands, retention and residency controls can diverge. No specific HIPAA/GDPR/DPA guarantees are documented in either profile, so the mismatch risk is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and copied into OpenHands
IF OpenHands forwards that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a DPA-approved deployment path
Minimize retention in mem0
Restrict OpenHands egress for regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
